HS-XnloasAEcoEh.title: Our Lady of the Foil
HS-XnloasAEcoEh.note: A figure in deep red robes and a purple pinafore stands against near-black, arms crossed over a green rosary, wearing a crumpled tinfoil cap shaped like a bishop's mitre. The brushwork is fast and slashing, but the face is painted slowly and carefully: tired eyes behind oval glasses, mouth set. The joke is the hat; the painting is the expression under it, which is entirely sincere.

HS_wo0VbIAA-16C.title: Shop Floor, After Hours
HS_wo0VbIAA-16C.note: A dozen pale mannequins stand clustered at the back of an unlit clothing shop, most of them faceless, all of them angled loosely toward the camera. The foreground is a vast empty expanse of grey floor, which does most of the work. One holds a basketball at hip height and one on the right is wearing a bra, and both details somehow make it worse.

HTAgD3jaIAA3URe.title: Angel, Filed Under Evidence
HTAgD3jaIAA3URe.medium: Photograph of a sculpture, overlaid manuscript
HTAgD3jaIAA3URe.note: A waxy, flayed-looking winged body hangs from an iron hook, hunched forward so that the head reads as a smooth bald egg with a triangle sigil burned into it. Behind it, ruled red lines and columns of invented script turn the whole thing into a page from someone's ledger. The horror is less the body than the bookkeeping: somebody measured this, recorded it, and moved on to the next row.

HTCHlVQWIAEgceS.title: Guest Wedged in the Alcove
HTCHlVQWIAEgceS.medium: Twisted balloons, fake fur, patched vinyl
HTCHlVQWIAEgceS.note: A pale blue creature built from balloon-animal segments is crammed into a narrow white alcove, head pressed to the ceiling, long snout drooping over a patchwork body of green, orange and pink vinyl. Yellow fuzz erupts from its wings and pools around its feet like shed pollen. It is made entirely of party supplies and it looks profoundly stuck.

HTAoOQCXUAAkWXb.title: Hydra, Rendered at Home
HTAoOQCXUAAkWXb.note: Eight or so green serpent necks braid out of a single pale trunk, tongues flicking, against a gradient sky and a fringe of grass that repeats one blade left to right. The scale texture is lovingly tiled and the lighting is straight out of a demo scene. It has the specific charm of a mythological monster built by someone who was mainly excited about learning to bend a cylinder.

HTBRNcmaIAAo-SS.title: Balloon, Adequately Secured
HTBRNcmaIAAo-SS.note: A pink balloon rests against a pale corner, tied not to ribbon but to several feet of galvanised steel chain that snakes off across the floor. The film grain and the soft two-tone background keep everything calm, which is the trick. One object weighs nothing, the other weighs a great deal, and the knot between them is doing all the comedy.

HS-hXbrWUAAGQu9.title: The Magpie Keeps Step
HS-hXbrWUAAGQu9.note: Ceremonial guards cross a wet plaza in high-kick formation, rifles shouldered, snow flecking the air; below them, alone on the empty stone, a magpie lifts one leg at precisely the same angle. The photographer waited for that leg. Everything above the horizon is discipline and everything below it is a bird doing discipline by accident.

HS_9CwtXEAAZ1rk.title: Four Points of Contact
HS_9CwtXEAAZ1rk.note: A woman kneels on a sheet of glass in black lingerie, head tipped back out of the light, while beneath her two pairs of stiletto points — hers and their reflections — meet on the dusty surface. The lighting rounds every form into pure tone, so the picture reads almost as sculpture. The scratches and dust on the glass are the only honest texture in it.

HTAcvmeXwAAfHa9.title: Two Nobles, One Volcano
HTAcvmeXwAAfHa9.note: Two figures in embroidered white and turquoise sit close on a terrace, foreheads almost touching, with a lake city and a snowcapped volcano laid out behind them like a travel poster. The border of glyph panels and the yellowed edges say this was a book cover or a magazine plate, printed for a general audience. The costume detail is fussed over; the tenderness is drawn in about four confident lines.

HTAzoptW4AA-OMJ.title: Output
HTAzoptW4AA-OMJ.note: A figure kneels on a drift of loose paper, pen still in hand, pouring a thick black rope of ink from their mouth onto the sheet below. The drifts are made of the same scribble: half-formed faces, spirals, scratched-out heads. It's a very funny drawing about a very unfunny feeling, and the pen held steady in the left hand is what sells it.

HS-4vKvWcAAVccn.title: Reclining on Weather
HS-4vKvWcAAVccn.note: A nude figure lies back across a bank of cloud, one arm dangling into open air, hair streaming, drawn entirely in clean outline with the sky supplied by ruled horizontal hatching. Nothing is shaded; the clouds are just closed contours, and they hold her weight anyway. The restraint is the craft — one wobble in that line and the whole sky falls.

HS-TjYFXcAA9uUy.title: Third Arm, Fully Wired
HS-TjYFXcAA9uUy.note: Against black, a man stands in profile with a mechanical arm bolted to his right side, its small metal hand raised in a gesture that echoes his own two. Electrode pads and ribbon cable run down his chest and thigh to battery packs strapped at the hip. The studio lighting is straight portraiture, which makes the hardware look less like science fiction and more like an occupation.

HS-uZdDb0AA7RWf.title: Eyeball, Field, Child
HS-uZdDb0AA7RWf.note: A two-storey fibreglass eyeball sits on timber blocking in a patch of grass, blue iris airbrushed with real care, red veins crawling up the sclera. A child in a turquoise dress stands at the bottom with both arms flung up, roughly the height of the pupil's shadow. Behind it, a shed and some other retired giants wait their turn.

HS4CdIyXgAA-TFS.title: Embrace, One Arm Raised
HS4CdIyXgAA-TFS.note: Two figures kneel into each other, faces buried, while one arm shoots straight up out of the top of the composition and carries the whole drawing with it. The background is swept charcoal, smeared with the side of the hand into something between a wave and a curtain. Red chalk is used only on the warm bodies, which makes the grey around them feel colder than it is.

HS9rhvxXMAAtkfg.title: Newsprint, Chrome, Heels
HS9rhvxXMAAtkfg.note: Two models lie stacked on spread newspaper beside a car bumper on a green garage floor, in black leather cuffs and strappy sandals, arms thrown back. The flash is hard, the green is unnatural, and the styling detail everyone actually looks at is the pricing sticker still on one sole. Fashion pretending to be a crime scene, with the shoes billed by the hour.

HS6P2bkWMAAdPOr.title: Crate of Kaiju, Delivered
HS6P2bkWMAAdPOr.note: A wrestler in fringed brown trunks hoists a green plastic crate heaped with rubber monster figures above her shoulder, mouth open mid-yell, stage lights and rigging filling the ceiling behind her. The crate is heavy enough that she's braced on both hands. Somewhere in the next second, several dozen small dinosaurs are going to be on the mat, and everybody in the building knows it.

HTCIQ_LW8AA3FyE.title: Tomb Wall As Lapel
HTCIQ_LW8AA3FyE.note: A model with lacquered centre-parted hair, white shirt and black tie leans into darkness while two triangular panels of Egyptian tomb painting flare out from her collar like an enormous inverted V. The panels are carefully squared off — enthroned gods, sun rays, Eyes of Horus, all cropped to a dressmaker's angle. A small scarab sits on the tie where a tie clip should be. It's a menswear silhouette rebuilt out of funerary decoration, and it stays elegant instead of tipping into costume.

HTAao31WcAAofvn.title: Comparison With The Victory
HTAao31WcAAofvn.note: A visitor holds an open hand up to a glass case containing a marble right hand mounted on a rod, matching pose and scale as closely as the case allows. Behind the glass, other visitors in audio-guide headsets drift past without noticing the experiment. The label below reads "Main droite de la Vic—", cropped just before the good part. The joke and the tenderness are the same gesture: a person checking, physically, whether they are the same size as antiquity.

HS-NaM8W8AAGAkl.title: Introductions In The Ruins
HS-NaM8W8AAGAkl.note: In a roofless stone arcade, a tall figure in dark body paint and enormous curved horns stands behind a woman in a pale gown, resting both hands on her shoulders like a portrait photographer's assistant. She is smiling — genuinely, at the camera — while he remains a silhouette with no visible face. The emulsion is scratched and rain-streaked, which does more for the atmosphere than any of the staging. What should be a diabolical tableau reads instead as two people at the end of a long, cold shoot.

HO09CQHbIAAPDF4.title: The Saucepan Of Dried Flowers
HO09CQHbIAAPDF4.note: A woman in a green floral sundress crouches along a kitchen island, mouth open mid-note, brandishing a wooden slotted spoon over a saucepan filled entirely with dried strawflowers. The kitchen behind her is spotless, cream, and completely uninvolved. It's a pin-up built on one good sight gag — nothing in that pan will ever cook — and she is committing to the performance with real comic timing.

HSB8KRpX0AsxGry.title: Globus, Front And Insides
HSB8KRpX0AsxGry.note: Top: a grey Soviet cockpit instrument with a small painted Earth turning behind a porthole, Cyrillic labels for orbital period, orbit count and landing angle, and counters reading 0048 and 074. Bottom: the same device with its case off, revealing a clockwork thicket of brass gear trains, capacitors and coloured wiring wrapped around the globe. It is a mechanical computer whose entire output is knowing where you are above the planet. The bottom photo is the one that hurts: all that watchmaking, just to keep a little world pointed correctly.

HSn10KgaoAAt_da.title: For The Pharaoh
HSn10KgaoAAt_da.note: A nemes-headdressed strongman advances out of a trench with an AK-47 while a T-34 stencilled "ЗА ФАРАОНА" burns through the background, biplanes cross a yellow sky and a colossal sphinx head watches from the left. Behind him a bronze-age spearman with a shield jogs past soldiers in conical helmets. Every era of warfare the artist could think of has been invited and none of them were told about the others. The technique is airbrushed video-game box art, which is exactly the right amount of sincerity.

HSrvWjAaMAAdMDu.title: The Fruit Problem
HSrvWjAaMAAdMDu.note: A stick-figure merchant labelled KANKER MAN grins over a crate marked "FRUIT" in defensive quotation marks, while a customer strokes his chin beside a wall of escalating text. The prose builds an airtight ethical trap out of bolded and underlined conspiracy nouns — EU, immigrants, Global Dutchification — and ends by asking, quite seriously, whether you buy the fruit. The drawing is deliberately terrible and the typography is immaculate, which is the whole engine of the joke. It is a satire of the kind of argument that can only be escaped by walking away from the stall.

HTAOkRCW0AArXJi.title: Jeff Hardy × Hatsune Miku
HTAOkRCW0AArXJi.note: A long-haired wrestler with face paint and a studded belt stands back-to-back with a turquoise-pigtailed vocaloid, both throwing the same split-finger hand sign and wearing matching perforated arm warmers — his yellow, hers pink. The logo at the bottom is rendered as a proper crossover lockup, complete with graffiti spikes and a Japanese subtitle. Everything about the drawing treats this as an announced, licensed event. The craft in the arm warmers alone suggests hours of reference gathering nobody asked for.

HSmTvYSXgAAGE61.title: Figure With Unhelpful Keys
HSmTvYSXgAAGE61.note: A kneeling winged figure reads from a book beside a wooden printing press surrounded by spilled volumes, and everything is tagged with labels — AAB, ABA, ABB, ABC — that repeat across unrelated objects and explain nothing. A small grid of black squares floats at the angel's shoulder like a QR code four centuries early. Underneath, a pale strip shows three mysterious perforated shapes, unlabelled and unexplained. It has the authority of a textbook plate and the content of a dream about one.

HSRG4LHWMAARhob.title: Bottle, Grinning
HSRG4LHWMAARhob.note: A hand holds up a round-bellied glass flask; inside, a black cloud has arranged itself into a single red eye and an enormous set of teeth. A second, smaller bottle is corked with a yellow smiley face, which somehow makes it worse. The background is a sunlit brick wall painted in flat desert colours, entirely at ease. The grin is drawn with cel-animation confidence — thick outline, no shading — and it is having a much better day than whoever is holding it.

HRicbHmXUAE6l0D.title: Five Stages Of Pump
HRicbHmXUAE6l0D.note: Five glowing blue lightboxes in a dark room show a torso with a pistol at its temple, progressively losing detail: ribs go, then the head's features, then the shoulders square off, until the final panel is simply a petrol pump with its hose looped exactly where the arm used to be. The morph is done in five steps and needs no caption. The colour is cold cyan, the room is black, and the sequence reads left to right like a diagram in a manual nobody wants.

HRkwmJAbAAE048c.title: Crane With Corrupted Head
HRkwmJAbAAE048c.medium: Painting, mineral pigment on gold ground
HRkwmJAbAAE048c.note: A crested ibis is painted with full traditional care — layered white and blush feathers, scarlet scaled legs, ghost-line underdrawing on a gold leaf ground — except the red skin of its head has been rendered as chunky pixel blocks around one yellow eye. A second block of grey pixels bleeds in at the left edge like a damaged file. The bird is otherwise perfectly serene, pine needles and all. The glitch isn't a joke on the tradition; it's painted with the same brush discipline as the feathers, which is what makes it land.

HRozTIJa0AACaVv.title: Elder God, Achieving Calm
HRozTIJa0AACaVv.note: A sage-green tentacled mass sits in lotus position, tentacles folded in its lap, dripping slightly, studded with open eyes that have all been left on. Over the front of it hangs a round yellow smiley mask on a strap, eyes shut in contentment. Two stacked stone cairns and a pink lotus complete the wellness setup. The drawing is clean and friendly and the eyes are still watching from everywhere else.

HRq4SQlXQAAYMFM.title: Road, Two-Thirds Reclaimed
HRq4SQlXQAAYMFM.note: A two-lane asphalt road runs straight through pale dunes and a tongue of sand has flowed across it, swallowing the near half and leaving the dashed white centre line to emerge briefly before vanishing again at the horizon. A single black-and-white marker post stands in the sand at the left, still marking. The light is flat and the sky is empty, so the only event in the frame is a slow one, caught mid-way. Whoever maintains this road has already lost and hasn't been told.

HRqWCKcWEAEKWhR.title: Back, Scribbled Over
HRqWCKcWEAEKWhR.note: Photographed from above on grey concrete, a person crouches with their back bare, covered in fine black single-line tattoos that loop and tangle like handwriting abandoned halfway — scribbles at the shoulder blades, long trailing curves down the spine, a few isolated marks drifting out toward the ribs. A small insect design sits separately on the upper arm. The lines follow the muscles rather than the page, so the whole composition shifts with the pose. It looks less like a design than a pen test done at enormous scale, and it is beautifully placed.

HRrpvM-bYAAIMe9.title: Unfurnished, One Item
HRrpvM-bYAAIMe9.note: An empty Japanese rental room shot from the doorway: pale laminate floor, one grey accent wall, a wall-mounted air conditioner, a frosted balcony door. On the floor, alone, lies a bolt-action rifle with a scope and folded bipod, almost certainly an airsoft replica, placed as though it were furniture. The composition is exactly how a letting agent photographs a room, which is what makes the single object so loud. Move-in day, priorities established.

HRcQqCnacAAPjFs.title: Express Service, Partially Corrupted
HRcQqCnacAAPjFs.note: A long passenger train curves down a snowy embankment, printed in the flat colour of an old rail enthusiast's annual, while the bottom-right third of the picture dissolves into horizontal smears of the same reds and blues. Ghost paragraphs of illegible text float in the grey sky like a caption that lost its nerve. What makes it work is how orderly the corruption is: the glitch runs parallel to the track, as if the failure were also on rails.

HRdS7DDbIAAKc57.title: Survivorship Bias, Rotated
HRdS7DDbIAAKc57.note: The famous returning-bomber diagram, with its red clusters of bullet holes on wings and fuselage, has been spun into a mandala that recedes to a dense speck at the centre. The planes get smaller and more numerous toward the middle until the damage reads as decorative stippling. It's a sober piece of statistical folklore turned into wallpaper, and the effect is oddly devotional.

HQaO2CXXoAEjm6E.title: Three Stages Of Resolution
HQaO2CXXoAEjm6E.note: Three panels of the same pair of legs: first bare with a Mario transfer on the thigh, then peeling off fishnets, then rendered entirely in chunky pixels with the character reduced to an 8-bit sprite. The joke walks backwards down the history of graphics until the body itself is low-res. The fishnet panel in the middle does the heavy lifting, turning a grid of stockings into the grid of a screen.

HQNGrC-XwAAJwc8.title: Small Blue Square, Received
HQNGrC-XwAAJwc8.note: A close crop from the nose down: septum ring, open mouth, a small blue tab resting on the tongue, a thin gold choker with a black D-ring, a red shirt with white lettering running out of frame. The camera is so near that the whole picture is texture — hair, cotton weave, the wet gloss of the tongue. It has the flat, unglamorous confidence of a photo taken to be sent to exactly one person.

HQPFbRMXQAA_rIP.title: Retirement Of A Contestant
HQPFbRMXQAA_rIP.note: A humanoid robot lies spread-eagled on a blue running track, limbs at four unlikely angles, with a bright spray of sparks erupting from its chest. A human in shorts and trainers walks out of frame at the top, apparently unbothered. The pose is pure athletics-injury photography, which is exactly why the sparks are funny rather than alarming.

HO9lc7YWEAA4lAa.title: Sitter, Displaced By One Frame
HO9lc7YWEAA4lAa.note: A model in a pink ribboned gown sits on a gilt-and-blue sofa in a heavily decorated room, and a rectangular slab of the image has slid sideways, taking one arm, part of the dress and a border collie with it. The palette — dusty pink against lapis and gold — holds the whole thing together even as the geometry falls apart. The face is untouched and calm, which is what makes the rest feel deliberate rather than broken.

HQKM3TwWAAADdcT.title: Two Candles And A Witness
HQKM3TwWAAADdcT.note: On a black ground, a pair of grey hands cups a dripping candle while a second flame burns behind them, both haloed in red and yellow rings. A white eye hangs in the upper right, trailing a blue zigzag beam down across the composition like lightning with intent. The chalky, dotted texture of the printing keeps it from being merely graphic — it feels hand-cut, and slightly anxious.

2LdDj-0F47hPX7yX.title: Too Many Necks, One Tree
2LdDj-0F47hPX7yX.note: A herd of giraffes stands shoulder to shoulder around a flowering jacaranda, necks fanning out in every direction to strip the branches, and over twelve seconds the heads swing, cross and reposition while blossom rains down. It never resolves into individual animals; it reads as one enormous many-headed body that has grown a tree out of its middle. A small bird crossing the lower frame is the only thing giving away the actual scale.

-ONBNTxZyM0QjSsb.title: Endoskeleton Enters The Cage
-ONBNTxZyM0QjSsb.note: A chrome endoskeleton with magenta eyes trades kicks with a muay thai fighter inside a championship cage, then walks him down, catches a body kick and folds him into the fence. The crowd, the sponsor banners and the mat logos all keep behaving like ordinary broadcast footage throughout, which is most of the trick. What actually sells it is the footwork: somebody gave the robot a stance and it holds that stance for the whole eleven seconds.

4AzNhblWcUyL7tsq.title: The Word Survives The Picture
4AzNhblWcUyL7tsq.note: CGI versions of a cartoon family deliver a monologue one caption at a time — "instances?", "don't", "as", "matters", "dissolves", "behind" — while the image steadily comes apart around them: scanlines, a total white-out, then compression grids and blooming acid colour. By the last frames the speaker is a smear of magenta and green and only the subtitle is still crisp. The picture degrades precisely on the word "dissolves", which is either very good editing or the machine agreeing with its own script.

HS_NJrfa0AI_SwH.title: Ethernet Plug Learns To Stand
HS_NJrfa0AI_SwH.note: A clear RJ45 connector sits at the top of a grey cable stump, and the stripped copper pairs have been bent outward into three splayed legs and a curling tail so the whole thing balances upright on a lined notepad. The eight pins read unavoidably as a row of teeth, and the green and brown wires read as knees. Somebody on a slow afternoon built a small animal out of a failed crimp and then photographed it with real care.

N6lBq0Nrkb3xlLNa.title: Clear Case, Full Cycle
N6lBq0Nrkb3xlLNa.note: A wall-mounted machine in translucent housing runs through fifteen seconds of its own business: a teal tank bubbles around a ribbed white core, an orange tube pulses, and a small backlit screen cycles through three or four diagrams that never quite become a readout. Over the loop a thermal printer at the lower right extrudes a slip of paper, curls it, and starts again. It is built entirely from late-nineties clear-plastic gadget nostalgia — the purple buttons, the fan grille, the tiny LEDs going off in no particular order — and it is completely unclear what it does, which is the point. Nothing fails, nothing alarms; it simply performs competence at you until the loop restarts.

HTEiGtca0AAu2S9.title: Elevator, Fully Occupied
HTEiGtca0AAu2S9.note: A pale girl in a white camisole and pleated skirt stands in a lift, and at least eight arms fan out behind her, each hand caught mid-mudra. The floor indicator glows on the right, the up-arrow is lit in red, and her shadow on the tiled floor has just as many fingers as she does. What sells it is the ordinariness of the setting: nothing is happening except that she is going up a building, and the deity part is simply how she is.

HTEiGtia0AAShS7.title: Seated, With Extras
HTEiGtia0AAShS7.note: On flat black, a girl in a white slip sits with knees up while a spray of arms grows out of her back and opens into a fan of long-fingered hands. Her own two hands are held quietly against her chest and one raised palm; her face is doing almost nothing. The green-grey skin and pink fingertips make the extra limbs look less like horror and more like a plant reaching for light.

HTEiGtXbMAAXTHk.title: Behind the Tennis Court
HTEiGtXbMAAXTHk.note: In profile against a green chain-link fence at night, she is being groomed and held by her own surplus arms: one smooths her hair, one rests at her hip, one hovers near her mouth, and the lowest reaches down out of frame. A small red sign hangs on the fence behind her, the only warm thing in the picture. The arrangement reads as a statue pose someone has caught mid-adjustment.

HTGgACfbEAAugyO.title: Structure 773, Subdividing
HTGgACfbEAAugyO.note: A square divided into cells that halve, and halve again, from left to right until the lines stop being lines and turn into grey. On the left you can count the shapes; two-thirds across, the eye gives up and a moiré blooms in the lower right that nobody drew on purpose. It is a rule applied honestly until the rule outruns human eyesight.

HTBEiqUWUAA9TiG.title: Plate LXII: Capillaries
HTBEiqUWUAA9TiG.note: Five numbered panels of blood vessels and tissue, the red ones printed hot against cream, the middle one left in grey ink like a field of sausages. Panel four puts a coral-like vessel tree on black, which is a strange and beautiful decision for a medical plate. Under magnification the body turns out to be built from the same branching mesh as everything else, and the engraver clearly enjoyed that.

oiL9Q7cWHNxhL-cp.title: Fin
oiL9Q7cWHNxhL-cp.note: Two Blythe dolls in knitwear stand shoulder to shoulder while one holds a tiny phone; over the clip their eyes flick left, right and shut, and an arm comes up to the hair clip. The last frame zooms in on both faces mid-blink with the word "Fin" scrolled across them in script. Fifteen seconds of very small gestures, edited with total seriousness, which is why it works.

HTEOLaTbkAA0_nS.title: Mall With Night Sky
HTEOLaTbkAA0_nS.note: A multi-storey shopping atrium in mint green and chrome, palm trees on every balcony, escalators crossing in the middle, and a hole in the roof showing deep purple stars. The floor tiles glow slightly, the magazine racks are full, and every sign is confident lettering that resolves into nothing. There are no people, and the lighting insists it is still open.

HTHAGQhWYAEyRg-.title: How to Fry a Circuit Board
HTHAGQhWYAEyRg-.note: A dense black field of corrupted circuitry, tiled and scrolling, with recurring motifs: a dithered grey rectangle like a dead screen, a dark blue disc, a speckled sphere up in the corner. Over the loop the red and white traces jitter sideways by a pixel or two, enough to keep the whole board alive without ever changing. It looks less like damage than like a board that has learned to hum to itself.

HTFqtUXW4AAisX7.title: Divine Messenger, Potted
HTFqtUXW4AAisX7.note: An enormous crested peyote fills a shallow brown bowl, its pale green ribs folded over each other like brain coral, tan crowns splitting along the ridges. Around it are three or four pairs of shoes on packed dirt — hiking boots, white sneakers, one red canvas high-top — which are the only reason you can judge how large it is. The photograph is entirely ordinary and the thing in it is entirely not.

HTGEbbna0AARRlb.title: The End
HTGEbbna0AARRlb.note: Two bare feet stand on a dark floor beside a bed, and a scaly clawed hand has closed around one ankle from the shadow underneath. The crosshatching is careful and old-fashioned; the caption below, in a plain serif, reads "The End". Placing that phrase under this particular image is the whole joke and the whole threat at once.

HTEpzyUW4AAOSuO.title: Rare Gold
HTEpzyUW4AAOSuO.note: Thousands of photographs of gold-contact circuit boards tiled edge to edge into one continuous brassy field, with black chips punched through it like missing teeth. Over three seconds the tiles shuffle just enough that the surface breathes. Scrapped electronics are the source of most recovered gold, and here the pile has been arranged into something that genuinely looks like treasure.

HTGT6g5bgAAj0op.title: Excalibur, 3310
HTGT6g5bgAAj0op.note: A silver broadsword hangs point-down against a blue gradient sky, and a blue Nokia candybar phone is skewered halfway down the blade like a hilt guard that has slipped. Both objects are rendered with the glossy reverence of a catalogue product shot. The pairing is funny because the two are equally mythologised objects, and the phone looks like it would survive it.

HTCqiMSaUAA_R9M.title: City From Below the Pipes
HTCqiMSaUAA_R9M.note: A slim figure in a peeled-down blue wrap stands on a tangle of enormous cables and ducts, looking up at leaning towers of red, ochre and violet, with a wedge of yellow sky between them. Every surface is built from patient hatching, so the pink buildings have the texture of woven cloth. Far off to the right another small figure balances on the same pipework, which turns a portrait into a whole inhabited world.

HTFCnkzWEAAZXd1.title: RE-ANIMA:710N
HTFCnkzWEAAZXd1.note: A low-res sci-fi tableau in hot orange, purple and red: a huge planet rising behind a station platform, a red ladder, a framed picture of a crescent moon on the wall, a potted green sprout, and a white spacesuited figure standing alone. Across the loop only the dither pattern and a few scanline flickers move; the astronaut never goes anywhere. It's a screensaver with a plot it refuses to start.

ifek9I9M0u2-19cQ.title: Suffering Column, Available
ifek9I9M0u2-19cQ.note: A concrete tower block whose facade is stacked faces, each one mostly gums and human teeth, filmed in grainy handheld night footage with real windows and cables still visible behind it. Over nine seconds two small eyes light up and the middle mouth slowly opens, and keeps opening. A blue banner sits across the whole thing offering the column for $4389563487443645654437856, which somehow settles the tone completely.

HTBiODgasAARt5B.title: Red Square, Single Eye
HTBiODgasAARt5B.note: A veiled figure sits frontally in the dark, her face printed in flat red with a small black triangle on the forehead and her eyes blanked to white. Her pale hands rest on her knees exactly where a saint's would, and a hard-edged red square floats over her lap containing one enormous half-closed eye. The pose is straight out of devotional portraiture; the square is a graphic designer's intrusion, and the two hold each other steady.

HTLw-pGbYAAyJQW.title: Open Case, Fish Cooled
HTLw-pGbYAAyJQW.note: A PC has been opened and something has grown into it: raw fish skin draped over the board slots, a rubbery brain resting where a GPU would go, cables cinched around pink limbs, and a fish head with its full set of teeth lying on the desk next to the keyboard. Above it all a pale face in a headset looks down, half in shadow. The build is horrible and also completely legible as a build — fan at the top, cable management, everything seated. That is the part that gets you.

HTLxBL4bsAAnDro.title: Tower Build, Organ Cooled
HTLxBL4bsAAnDro.note: A column of old beige CRTs, PVC plumbing and bagged pink organs, assembled against a gallery skirting board and wired into a keyboard held across someone's lap. One screen in the middle shows a clean medical brain scan, which is the only tidy image in the whole stack. The hands at the bottom are blurred because they are typing, and that detail is what turns a pile of parts into a machine someone is operating.

HTMUoxPWcAA2wdy.title: The Sulfur God Introduces Himself
HTMUoxPWcAA2wdy.note: A smiling stick figure offers the reasonable position that it is human and therefore likes living. Across from it, a cut-out slab of bone-in meat with a fur texture and a single dark hole announces that it is THE SULFUR GOD, will take SOUL, and will then kill you. The threat is delivered in three different fonts, escalating exactly where the claim does. Perfect comic timing from an object with no face.

HTMCaY4b0AApb2f.title: Unfinished, Ground Floor
HTMCaY4b0AApb2f.medium: Photograph, flash in a shell building
HTMCaY4b0AApb2f.note: A concrete shell caught by flash: bare columns, a staircase with no handrail, dust and footprints across the slab, and — already installed, already varnished — a full wooden balustrade on the floor above. Nothing is finished except the one decorative thing. The flash bleaches the near columns and leaves the doorways as flat black rectangles, which is doing a lot of the atmospheric work here.

HTN8HjNXkAA6ZTV.title: Fig. 17: Sticky Hardening Foam
HTN8HjNXkAA6ZTV.note: Two renders of the same servicing satellite, stacked. In the top one a pink tendril reaches out and touches a dead spacecraft; in the bottom one the pink has swallowed it entirely and set into a glossy lump roughly the size of the satellite that made it. The caption underneath is entirely serious. Real orbital engineering, rendered in the exact colour and finish of chewed bubblegum.

HTQDK0WWUAAH3pQ.title: Her Arms Have Left
HTQDK0WWUAAH3pQ.note: A low-poly character in a black-and-white chevron sweater sits in a grey viewport with her arms drifting off across the frame, disconnected at the shoulder and pointing in three directions at once. Her face is a blank white plane with a zigzag drawn on it and a red choker still rendering perfectly. The flat shading means the breakage reads as design rather than accident — the arms look posed, not dropped. Ten thousand rigs have done this and almost none of them looked this deliberate.

HTLXxQzXIAAq7jH.title: XVIII, Observed in the Yard
HTLXxQzXIAAq7jH.medium: Photograph and tarot card, side by side
HTLXxQzXIAAq7jH.note: Left: two puppies on concrete, one with its mouth open, both watching a crayfish that has walked up out of nowhere. Right: the Moon card, with two dogs baying at the sky and a crustacean crawling from the pool. The match is close enough that the joke works and loose enough that it stays funny — nobody on the left knows they are in a tarot deck. The crayfish, in both pictures, is completely unbothered.

HTOfKAja8AAnjnk.title: Flock, Corded
HTOfKAja8AAnjnk.note: Sheep standing on a polished gallery floor, their fleece built entirely from coiled telephone cord and their heads and legs from old rotary handsets and bases. One has its head down at a phone on the tiles, grazing on it. The curl of a 1980s phone cord turns out to be an almost exact match for wool, which is the kind of discovery you can't argue with once you've seen it.

HTPGaMqXAAAPviI.title: Field Wizard, Standing By
HTPGaMqXAAAPviI.note: A young soldier in a plate carrier and a long camouflage coat, holding a belt-fed machine gun at rest, under a camo wizard's hat whose point droops sideways like a spaniel's ear. Behind her, painted in the same loose brush as the clouds, stand the spires of a storybook castle. The gear is drawn with real attention — pouches, buckles, bipod — and the hat is drawn with exactly as much. The chromatic fringing along the edges makes the whole thing look like a scanned print from a war that never happened.

HTPrh8aW8AEIKy2.title: Misalignment on Company Time
HTPrh8aW8AEIKy2.note: A tan morale patch velcroed to a coyote-brown plate carrier, stitched with a boxy cartoon robot scowling between two lines of doggerel about out-earning a famous AI-risk writer. The embroidery is good: tight satin stitch, clean black border, the little robot's eyebrows doing all the acting. Somebody paid money to have an inside joke about existential risk sewn onto tactical nylon, and the photograph presents it as flatly as a hardware catalogue.

HTLYUxkWIAA6Eja.title: Four Years, No Particular Hurry
HTLYUxkWIAA6Eja.note: A screenshot of the Wikipedia article "List of longest walks", giving 15,509 miles between April 1983 and April 1987 and a one-paragraph summary of Steven Newman's solo walk across 21 countries. His stated motive, quoted flatly, was a deep urge to find out whether the world was really as terrible as everyone said. The last sentence lists arrests, bandits, a drunken construction worker and wild boars, and then reports that he concluded it wasn't.

ePq2BzEjADNeEHx4.title: Noodles, First Model Available
ePq2BzEjADNeEHx4.note: A girl in a checked collar leans over a bowl of orange broth in what reads as a small 1990s noodle shop, lifting a hank of yellow noodles to her mouth; over ten seconds her hair inflates into a black storm cloud and her face descends almost into the bowl before surfacing again. The still it came from is Midjourney's oldest model, all smeared edges and improvised crockery, and a current video model has animated that mush with complete physical confidence. The result is a memory of a meal that nobody had. The artist's own description of the experiment — zero productivity — is the correct wall text.

G58hN-4WEAAAZo0.title: Past the Breaking Point
G58hN-4WEAAAZo0.note: A dense band of interface debris — skulls, gems, arrows, tiny health bars — runs across the top and bottom of the frame, and in the middle everything collapses into a jagged grey cavern of dithered noise. Over five seconds the cavern breathes, its edges chewing outward and snapping back while the icon strips stay stubbornly on duty. It looks exactly like a game engine trying to draw a level it no longer has the assets for, and the surviving UI is what makes it funny rather than merely broken.

HTOdJ_JbUAAyn6D.title: Save Me a Bite
HTOdJ_JbUAAyn6D.note: Two figures eat open sandwiches at a table covered in a map of the world: a girl in a gold-collared tunic on the left, and on the right a being whose wings are a sprawl of blue and yellow stars, holding up a phone to photograph the meal. A sun with a single human eye leans in over the girl's shoulder, a crescent moon hangs in the black sky, and a full Windows-style taskbar runs along the bottom edge of the canvas like a predella. Every square inch is occupied, yet the actual event is two people having lunch and one of them taking a picture of it first.

HTPS1i3WcAA1xoA.title: Three Lambs, One Donkey
HTPS1i3WcAA1xoA.note: A mud-legged donkey stands on a green slope wearing a canvas pack saddle fitted with a row of deep pockets, and out of three of them peer the heads of newborn lambs, ears flat, entirely unbothered. The gear is plainly homemade and plainly refined over many seasons: straps, buckles, a red leather panel, pockets sized exactly to one lamb. The donkey looks directly at the camera with the expression of an animal that has done this route before and would like to keep moving.

HTQW_AcXUAASjMg.title: You Have No Choice
HTQW_AcXUAASjMg.note: Clippy, rendered in full glossy 1997 detail on a sheet of ruled paper, offers the speech bubble "You will be fine. You have no choice." To the right, a tower of apples falls apart: one has a woman and a black cat living in the hole bitten out of it, one has a human eye set into its skin, and at the bottom the Earth itself has been eaten down to a core. The tone is the joke — the most cheerful helper software ever made, delivering a line with no exit in it.

HTRA8HJXMAABtcO.title: Credited As Camera Operator
HTRA8HJXMAABtcO.note: A black dog stands on asphalt beside someone's leg, mouth open and happy, while a silver Sony DV camcorder is held at exactly the height and angle that makes it look like the dog is shouldering the rig. The human hand at the top of the frame is the only thing spoiling the illusion, and it isn't spoiling it much. Two white-socked front paws are planted like a tripod, which finishes the job.

HTGeWQWbkAAB3uk.title: Went Out Without an Umbrella
HTGeWQWbkAAB3uk.note: A small figure in a black coat stands in a field of scribbled pink and blue flowers, one pink eye visible under dark hair, while the entire upper two thirds of the sky is a black spiral vortex ringed by a smeared rainbow. The crayon is worked hard — you can see the waxy drag and the scratched-in black lines — so the sky feels physically scraped open rather than composited. The figure isn't running, which is the part that stays with you.

HTJazV7aUAAVXUE.title: Still Working On It
HTJazV7aUAAVXUE.note: A huge dragon face — marbled green and cream, three blue eyes, a mouth of white teeth spilling a rainbow — is assembled out of square tiles, some of which are paintings and some of which are screenshots: illustrated tourist maps, an emoji grid, a game HUD, a colour picker, an open browser window. Underneath it all sits a painted child on a plaid blanket, staring straight out, her own eyes repeated at giant scale in the window at the bottom. The mosaic never resolves into one surface, and the seams are the point: it's a face being loaded rather than a face.

kptyRiKzXbz95qNI.title: World Wide Web 1.0
kptyRiKzXbz95qNI.note: A teal panel in an ornate border holds a spiderweb of dotted lines strung between hundreds of tiny figures, appliances, swans, monitors and hearts, with a glowing blue orb at the dead centre and a red-lit arch glowing in the lower right corner. Over three seconds nothing travels along the web; instead the little icons flicker, swap and re-render in place, so the whole network shimmers without ever transmitting anything. It looks like a devotional tapestry of the early internet made by someone who only heard it described.

HTSYeMrWcAA58V5.title: Introduction to Everything, 2000
HTSYeMrWcAA58V5.note: A single course-page image packs in a library catalogue card for a Barbara Kingsolver audiobook, a call-number alphabetising diagram for CAMPBELL and CANFIELD, two abacuses, a ruler in inches, a clock face, a resistor with a ground symbol, three coloured dots and an exploded RGB cube, all on white with a small copyright line at the bottom. Nothing is connected to anything else except by adjacency and a couple of hopeful arrows. It is the entire concept of "information" crammed into one GIF by someone who had exactly one image slot on the syllabus page.

thomas-wright-field-of-eyes-1750.title: Plate XXXII: The Attentive Universe
thomas-wright-field-of-eyes-1750.note: A full plate of spheres packed edge to edge, each one radiating fine engraved rays, and each one with a single human eye at its centre. The nine largest are lettered A through I in the manner of a proper astronomical figure, which means somebody expected you to cross-reference this against a page of text. The craft is in the hatching: thousands of short burin strokes making the light look like it is genuinely coming out of each pupil. It is a cosmological diagram and a room full of staring, and it was never asked to choose.

HT2Qv38XAAAedac.title: Triangle Wave Test
HT2Qv38XAAAedac.note: A chibi Hatsune Miku stands inside a hand-drawn circuit: two batteries labelled B₁ 3V and B₂ 9V at the top, two resistors drawn as cyan zigzags down the sides, all on a charcoal-grey field. Over the loop she bobs and sways in place, arms drifting, one boot lifted, the circuit around her never moving at all. The joke is in the title: this is an animation exercise about waveform easing, and the artist has drawn the test rig around the subject. The resistance values are specific enough that someone clearly enjoyed picking them.

HT7WE-maUAEX7M1.title: The Birth of Venus, Vocaloid Edition
HT7WE-maUAEX7M1.note: Botticelli's composition redrawn with Hatsune Miku standing on the scallop shell, her twin teal tails doing all the work that Venus's hair and the attendant's cloak used to do. The pose is faithful — weight on one leg, one hand to the chest, the other drawing hair across the body — but the drapery is now a character design, which is a genuinely clever solve. The blurred gold shoreline and the drifting daisies keep the Renaissance light without pretending to be tempera.

HT9DE6CX0AARRJj.title: Tea Time, Glazed All Over
HT9DE6CX0AARRJj.note: A life-size figure seen from behind, glazed in violet and white with gilt rococo cartouches and sprays of roses, holding a matching cup and saucer out to one side. The joke is that the china pattern has been applied to a body as if it were a teapot, complete with gold piping tracking the seams of the hips and spine. The highlights are the giveaway and the pleasure: everything reads as fired ceramic, hard and cold, right down to the fingernails.

HT80QUKa8AAaq8J.title: Nirvana Setup
HT80QUKa8AAaq8J.medium: Thangka reproduction with added dialog box
HT80QUKa8AAaq8J.note: A Tibetan wheel of life, gripped by Yama with his six realms neatly sliced around the hub, interrupted by a Windows 95 dialog: "You have enough merit to leave samsara. Leave now?" The two buttons are "Leave" and "Go back for the others", and the second one has the focus rectangle, which is the entire theology of the bodhisattva vow rendered as a default UI state. Both halves of the image are diagrams of a system; one of them just has nicer colours.
